podcast.body: A ruminative new single dropped without warning on David Bowie's 66th birthday, January 8th, 2013, ending his decade-long unofficial retirement. It bubbled under the Hot 100, driven mostly by iTunes downloads, and cracked the top 10 in the UK. Musically, it was a gentle rumination unlike any prior Bowie lead single, wistfully looking back on his life and suggesting a somber tone for the upcoming "The Next Day" album. "On January 8th, 2013, David Bowie's 66th birthday, he ended his unofficial retirement. With no prior warning, Bowie dropped a ruminative new single called Where Are We Now?"

podcast.body: This song casually appeared online on January 8, 2013, coinciding with Bowie's 66th birthday, and immediately caused a global sensation as the world realized Bowie was making a comeback. Its release preceded the album *The Next Day* by two months, signaling his return in "fine, fine form." "A song called Where They Now Casually Appeared Online. And the whole world screamed at once. What? Bowie is back?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
